text:
jordan: Drafting a different angle for the benchmark narrative ter talking to AE leads: they want a single, simple chart that non-technical execs can scan during discovery. Idea: combine latency p95 and cost-per-1k-tokens into one two-axis micro-plot with colored zones (fast+cheap = green). Thoughts?

nina: love it. also add a tiny callout showing baseline model on public cloud vs Redwood Dedicated config. Visual should have 3 datapoints: baseline hosted, redwood-hosted-optimized, redwood-dedicated.

kevin: Technical nuance: we need to be explicit about identical prompts and max_tokens cap, otherwise analysts will call out differences. put "+appendix" footnote in the slide.

jordan: Good call. For messaging briefs: headline option 1 = "Fast where it matters. Cheap where it counts." option 2 = "Tradeoffs made visible: latency and unit-economics." Which lands for sales decks?

nina: Option 1 resonates more with AE. It's punchier.

kevin: For the press tweet, compress to: "Real-world chat: p95 down 3x, tokens per-$ improved 40% vs baseline. See notes."

ops-bot: Reminder: Compliance needs a short methodology blurb before sending to press. Add to checklist.

jordan: Action items: 1) design to produce 1 two-axis micro-plot + 1 single stat card by Thu EOD @design-bot 2) comp language for AE one-pager by Wed @jordan 3) methodology footnote draft by Thu @kevin

design-bot: Uploaded first comp: https://designs.redwood/viz/two_axis_comp_v1.png. Feedback welcome.

nina: I'll queue the AEs for quick feedback session Friday.

kevin: I'll start the methodology appendix and share raw CSVs.

jordan: Great. Let's lock this as the canonical discovery visual if comps look good.
